subject: Literacy
title: Words for food and market
objectives: Children will name fruits, vegetables and market things.
Children will ask for something using a short phrase.
content: Naming fruits and vegetables, market people and things, and asking for things politely.
teachingActivities: Use real or toy foods from the local market; model "Good morning ma, I want two oranges, please"; give children time to say the word and accept gestures; build the market corner over the week.
learnerActivities: Name fruits, vegetables and market items and ask for something with a short phrase.
resources: Real or toy oranges, mangoes, tomatoes, yams and onions
assessment: Observe whether each child names six fruits or vegetables and asks for an item with a short phrase.
expectedOutcomes: Names at least six fruits or vegetables.
Uses a short phrase to ask for an item.
crossCurricular: Understanding the World: community and market

lessons.title: Fruits we like
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will name three fruits and say which one they like.
successCriteria: Names or points to an orange, a mango and a banana
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar foods and objects and use two words to ask for something.
resources: Real or toy orange, mango and banana
lessons.starter: Show a ripe mango and say "This is a mango. Mmm." Ask "What do you like?"
teacherActivities: Hold up each fruit and say its name. Pass it round to touch.
Say "Where is the orange?" and wait.
Let each child choose a fruit and say its name.
learnerActivities: Children touch and say the name.
Child points to the orange.
Child points to a fruit or says its name.
Child holds up the fruit and names it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hold up each fruit and say its name. Pass it round to touch. Children: Children touch and say the name.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Where is the orange?" and wait. Children: Child points to the orange.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which fruit do you like?" Children: Child points to a fruit or says its name.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a fruit and say its name. Children: Child holds up the fruit and names it.

practical.title: Fruit basket
steps: Put three fruits in a basket.
Each child takes one and names it.
practical.safety: If real fruit is used, wash it, check for allergies and keep it for looking and touching unless eating is planned. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Offer two fruits and say the name with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend what colour the fruit is.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the fruits back and say "Thank you, fruits."
lessons.homeConnection: Name the fruits at home and let your child choose one.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name three fruits and say which one they like" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Vegetables and yams
lessons.subject: Literacy
successCriteria: Names or points to a tomato, an onion and a yam
Says a word for a vegetable
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar foods and objects and use two words to ask for something.
resources: Real or toy tomatoes, onions and yams
lessons.starter: Hold up a tomato and say "Red tomato." Ask "What colour is it?"
teacherActivities: Show each vegetable, name it and let children touch it.
Hide one under the cloth and ask "What is it?"
Sort the fruits and vegetables into two baskets.
Ask "What do we cook with?" and show the pictures.
learnerActivities: Children touch and name.
Child feels or guesses the name.
Child puts each in a basket.
Child points to a vegetable.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each vegetable, name it and let children touch it. Children: Children touch and name.
Step 2. Teacher: Hide one under the cloth and ask "What is it?" Children: Child feels or guesses the name.
Step 3. Teacher: Sort the fruits and vegetables into two baskets. Children: Child puts each in a basket.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What do we cook with?" and show the pictures. Children: Child points to a vegetable.

practical.title: Fruit and vegetable sort
steps: Each child picks an item and names it.
Put it in the fruit or vegetable basket.
practical.safety: Wash real vegetables first and supervise. Keep onions away from eyes and wash hands after touching.

differentiation.support: Use two items and say the names for the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name a vegetable they eat at home.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Sorts fruit and vegetables with support
lessons.conclusion: Put away the vegetables and wash hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Name the vegetables when you cook or shop together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name three vegetables" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: At the market
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will name market people and things.
successCriteria: Names a seller and a buyer
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar foods and objects and use two words to ask for something.
lessons.starter: Put on the apron and say "I am the seller. Come to my market!" Hold up a basket.
teacherActivities: Show the stall and name each thing: seller, buyer, basket, coins.
Say "Good morning, ma" and show a greeting to the seller.
Show how a buyer points to what they want.
Let each child be the buyer and take an item.
learnerActivities: Children point and say each word.
Children say good morning.
Child points to an item.
Child names the item.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the stall and name each thing: seller, buyer, basket, coins. Children: Children point and say each word.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Good morning, ma" and show a greeting to the seller. Children: Children say good morning.
Step 3. Teacher: Show how a buyer points to what they want. Children: Child points to an item.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child be the buyer and take an item. Children: Child names the item.

practical.title: Market corner
steps: Set up the stall with baskets of toy foods.
Children take turns as the seller and buyer.
Say the names of items together.
practical.safety: Use toy foods only and keep coins large. Supervise turn-taking and keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Be the seller and help the child to point and name.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the seller and greet a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Close the market and say goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Take your child to the market and name the things and the people you see.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name market people and things" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Asking politely
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will ask for an item using a short phrase.
successCriteria: Says I want and the item name with please
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar foods and objects and use two words to ask for something.
lessons.starter: Say "Good morning, ma. Two oranges, please." Hand over a toy coin and say "Thank you."
teacherActivities: Model the phrases "I want an orange, please" and "Thank you".
Play the buyer and let a child play the seller.
Let each child be the buyer and ask for an item.
learnerActivities: Children repeat.
Child serves and says "here you are".
Child asks with a short phrase.
Child asks or serves.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Model the phrases "I want an orange, please" and "Thank you". Children: Children repeat.
Step 2. Teacher: Play the buyer and let a child play the seller. Children: Child serves and says "here you are".
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child be the buyer and ask for an item. Children: Child asks with a short phrase.
Step 4. Teacher: Change roles and play again. Children: Child asks or serves.

practical.title: Market role play
steps: Set up the stall with toy foods.
Take turns as buyer and seller.
The buyer asks politely and says thank you.
practical.safety: Use toy foods and large coins only. Supervise each pair and keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Say the phrase with the child and let them choose the item.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to ask for two different items.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you say when you ask?
What do you say after you get it?

expectedOutcomes: Asks for an item with a short phrase
lessons.conclusion: Close the market and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child ask for what they want in a shop or at the market using please.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "ask for an item using a short phrase" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 market check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child names market items and asks politely.
successCriteria: Names at least six fruits or vegetables
Asks for an item with a short phrase
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name familiar foods and objects and use two words to ask for something.
lessons.starter: Sing "Market, market, come and see" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: fruit, vegetables and market role play.
At each station ask "What is this?" and "What do you want?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every five minutes.
Child names the item and asks.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: fruit, vegetables and market role play. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What is this?" and "What do you want?" Children: Child names the item and asks.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Market stations
practical.safety: Use toy foods and large coins. Supervise each station and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and accept gestures.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to run the stall.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names fruits and vegetables; names market people; asks politely with a short phrase.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
Names market items and asks politely
lessons.conclusion: Close the market and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Practise asking politely in a shop or at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child names market items and asks politely" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
